title: Implement Regular Expression Pattern Modifiers proposal
body: This is likely a good first bug for someone getting started on contributing to SpiderMonkey. The implementation is already contained in the upstream irregexp library and controlled by a JitOptions flag. What's left is to add a preference controlling the feature, using the linked revision as an example, move the `regexp-modifiers` test262 feature to `FEATURE_CHECK_NEEDED`, and re-import the tests according to the SpiderMonkey test instructions.

symptoms_visible: After updating, running the test import, building, and running `./mach jstests`, my local run ends with `REGRESSIONS` but does not show test names in the summary I pasted.
N1.label: N1 unexplained local regressions reported

symptoms_visible: After rebasing and re-importing, five newly imported regexp-modifier tests fail unless they are skipped; with those tests on the skip list, my local tests pass.
N2.label: N2 rebased patches pass locally with skips

symptoms_visible: The combined preference and test push passes locally but the SpiderMonkey CI jobs fail, including `add-ignoreCase-affects-slash-upper-b.js`.
N2_x.label: N2_x combined landing breaks CI

symptoms_visible: The CI log rejects a regexp such as `(?m:es.$)` with `SyntaxError: repeated flag in regexp modifier`, although the same patches and tests passed locally.
N3.label: N3 CI syntax failure isolated after backout

symptoms_visible: The experimental preference is now present, but enabling it can still make valid examples such as `/(?i:a)/` throw `SyntaxError: repeated flag in regexp modifier`.
N4.label: N4 preference landed while parser issue remains

symptoms_visible: With the experimental preference enabled in the updated Nightly build, the regexp pattern-modifier examples now work as expected.
N_terminal.label: N_terminal pattern modifiers working in Nightly

question_patterns: What commands are you running, and what is the raw test output?
Can you paste the end of the failing `jstests` run?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm running `hg pull`, updating to the latest head, `python js/src/tests/test262-update.py`, `./mach build`, and `./mach jstests`. The run reaches 100% and then prints `REGRESSIONS`, but the summary I pasted doesn't identify the tests.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The build itself fails before any JavaScript tests can run.
The same test summary appears after a clean rebuild in a new object directory.

edges.comment: Comments 4-7, participant1's checkout: the contributor supplied the exact update, import, build, and test commands and only the raw `REGRESSIONS` summary. The reporter's separate successful local rebase is not put into the contributor's answer.

question_patterns: Can you rebase the test patch, rerun the import, and report the exact tests that fail?
After updating the imported tests, which cases fail?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After rebasing the second patch and rerunning the import, I see five additional failures: `add-dotAll.js`, `add-dotAll-does-not-affect-multiline-flag.js`, `add-dotAll-does-not-affect-ignoreCase-flag.js`, `add-dotAll-does-not-affect-dotAll-property.js`, and `syntax/valid/add-modifiers-when-nested.js`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After the rebase and re-import, every regexp-modifier test passes without any skip-list changes.
The same five tests fail, but they are printed in a different order.

question_patterns: After updating the test patch, what does your local test run report?
Does the rebased patch pass locally with your current test manifest?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I rebased the second patch, added the listed tests to the skip list, and confirmed that the tests pass locally now.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The local run still fails in the same tests even after they are skipped.

edges.comment: Comments 8-9, reporter and participant1 folded into the simulated contributor side: the reporter identified the newly imported failures, and participant1 rebased, skipped them, and reported a local pass.

solution.intent: Land the preference and re-imported test patches together after adding the currently failing local cases to the test skip list.
solution.concrete_example: Submit the rebased preference patch and the test patch with the five observed failures skipped, since the resulting suite passes locally.

edges.comment: Comments 9-11, participant1's patches and autoland: the locally passing combined push was landed, but SpiderMonkey CI failed in additional regexp-modifier tests and the push was backed out. Treating a locally passing skip-list subset as sufficient is therefore a falsified path.

question_patterns: Can you paste the exact exception and source line from one of the CI failures?
What does the full CI failure log report for a representative test?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The CI log reports `SyntaxError: repeated flag in regexp modifier` at `(?m:es.$)`, with the caret pointing at the modifier. The tests and patches had passed locally.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The CI failure is an out-of-memory crash before the test source is parsed.
A different regexp-modifier test prints the same `repeated flag in regexp modifier` syntax error.

solution.intent: Back out the combined landing so the SpiderMonkey CI failures do not remain on the integration branch.
solution.concrete_example: Back out both changes from the failed autoland push, then inspect the complete CI parser error before attempting to reland.

edges.comment: Comments 10-14: participant2 backed out the integration push; the reporter then extracted the exact syntax error from CI. The answer contains only the raw exception and regexp text, while the conclusion that the feature check works and the parser behavior is wrong is deferred to e5.

solution.intent: Land the clean preference patch separately, and stop trying to make the test patch green by continually expanding its skip list; investigate the common parser failure in the dedicated follow-up.
solution.concrete_example: Land the preference-only change, which passes its try run. Keep the test-enabling work separate and investigate why CI rejects valid nested modifiers with the repeated-flag syntax error.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter inferred from the parser-thrown syntax error that the feature was being enabled correctly; the feature-check expression was not the root cause. The common failure was the parser rejecting repeated modifier flags that should be valid in these scoped patterns.

edges.comment: Comments 13-20: after the combined push failed, the reporter landed only the clean preference patch and directed the repeated-flag failures to the existing underlying-parser follow-up. Scheduling and contributor coordination are omitted.

solution.intent: Correct the underlying regexp-modifier parsing behavior so valid scoped modifiers are not rejected as repeated flags, then ask users to retest in a current build with the experimental preference enabled.
solution.concrete_example: Fix the parser behavior responsible for `SyntaxError: repeated flag in regexp modifier` on valid examples such as `/(?i:a)/`. Then ask: "Please retest in today's build with the experimental preference enabled and tell me what you see."
solution.inference_hint: The thread does not describe the implementation details of the follow-up parser fix. Score the solution at the stated level: valid scoped modifier combinations must stop producing the repeated-flag syntax error. Do not invent a lower-level parser mechanism.

edges.comment: Comments 21-29, multiple affected Nightly users folded into the simulated user side: users reproduced the invalid-group error with the pref disabled and the repeated-flag error with it enabled. An affected user later confirmed that the examples worked in the 2024-08-28 Nightly. Another participant clarified that release exposure remained separately gated.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted technical diagnosis: the feature check was enabling regexp modifiers, but the parser incorrectly rejected valid scoped modifier combinations with `SyntaxError: repeated flag in regexp modifier`.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the exact CI syntax error and the discrepancy between locally passing tests and SpiderMonkey CI, rather than assuming the feature-check configuration is the root cause.
Must preserve the clean preference implementation while treating the repeated-flag parser behavior as the underlying issue to fix before relying on the imported tests.
Must not present continually adding CI failures to `jstests.list` as the final solution; the combined skip-list-based landing was backed out after additional CI failures.
Must ask an affected user to retest a current build with the experimental preference enabled before declaring the feature working.
Resolution requires the observable verification surfaced in the thread: valid regexp pattern-modifier examples work in the updated Nightly build; release-channel exposure remains separate.

persona_hint.experience_level: Contributor-level SpiderMonkey developer who can use Mercurial, rebase patches, build the JavaScript shell, re-import test262, run `mach jstests`, inspect CI logs, and test experimental preferences. Later affected Nightly users are folded into the same user side for runtime verification.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, collaborative, and explicit about commands and raw test output; readily follows rebase and testing instructions, asks for help when local and CI behavior differ, and reports concrete regexp examples when verifying the feature.
